plan_title: Tundra SGS Subpart RR Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification (MRV) Plan
ama_definition: The permitted Broom Creek Area of Review (20-year simulated plume rounded to 40-acre tracts plus a 1-mile buffer) serves as the AMA for both the Broom Creek and Deadwood–Black Island storage facilities, since it encloses the calculated t=20 plume plus half-mile buffer for both (p12-14).
mma_definition: The same Broom Creek AOR serves as the MMA, because it exceeds the t+10 plume plus a half-mile buffer for both formations (p15-16).
leakage_pathways_rated_significant: Surface equipment and the flowline are called the likeliest leakage pathway during injection, including a low-probability catastrophic wellhead/flowline failure; injection and monitoring wellbores are rated unlikely; faults, seismicity, lateral migration and diffuse seal leakage are rated very unlikely to nearly impossible (p17, p19, p24-27, p29).
baseline_summary: A pre-injection baseline period of at least one year covering all four seasons: surface water, soil gas, shallow groundwater from selected domestic wells and a USGS Fox Hills well (sampled August 2021), formation water, saturation logs and casing inspection logs in injection and monitoring wells, a baseline 3D seismic survey, seismometer stations installed a year before injection, and an InSAR feasibility study (p16, p31-32, p36-37).
reporting_summary: Annual Subpart RR report with the mass balance (Equations RR-5, RR-10, RR-12) filed with other GHG reports by end of March; records kept at least 3 years; events communicated to the UIC program director within 24 hours if warranted and a formal AOR review submitted every 5 years to the state; no commitment to publish measurement data (p35, p37-39, p41-42).

rows.detail: Volumetric flowmeter at metering station M2 used for the mass balance, flowmeters and pressure/temperature transducers at each metering station and on each well flowline; CO2 stream composition sampled quarterly.
rows.location: Metering stations M1 and M2 and each injection well flowline
rows.evidence_quote: Flowmeters and temperature and pressure transducers will be installed at each metering station.

rows.detail: Real-time surface pressure and temperature gauges on injection wells and flowline, tracked by an automated SCADA system with alarms and shutoff devices; readings compared with set points and history-matched model.
rows.location: Each injection well and the CO2 flowline
rows.trigger_or_response: Deviation from set points triggers an automatic data flag; field personnel investigate; shutoff device activates if thresholds exceeded.
rows.evidence_quote: if the injection pressure, temperature, or rate measurements deviate significantly from the specified set points, then a data flag will be automatically triggered

rows.detail: Wellhead pressure gauges monitor tubing-casing annular pressure as part of real-time well integrity monitoring.
rows.trigger_or_response: Threshold exceedance alerts operator and activates shutoff device.
rows.evidence_quote: Pressure gauges will be installed on the wellhead to monitor annular pressure between tubing and casing.

rows.detail: Annular pressure tests and EM/sonic casing inspection logs: before injection, every 5 years for Broom Creek injectors, annually for Deadwood–Black Island, during workovers, before P&A; monitoring wells every 5 years.
rows.trigger_or_response: Substandard conditions prompt timely response under the corrosion and mechanical integrity program.

rows.detail: Downhole pressure and temperature gauges in injection wells and the in-zone monitoring well NRDT-1 (real time; bimonthly post-injection), surface gauges on monitoring wells, and pressure falloff tests every 5 years.
rows.location: Injection wells and NRDT-1 monitoring well about 2 miles northeast
rows.trigger_or_response: Pressures that diverge from the history-matched model are investigated; model recalibrated.
rows.evidence_quote: continuous, automated pressure and temperature monitoring in the injection zone

rows.detail: Routine visual inspections of wellheads, flowline and surface equipment, weekly during injection and quarterly post-injection, looking for white clouds and ice from CO2 releases.
rows.trigger_or_response: Discovery of an event triggers the emergency remedial and response plan.
rows.evidence_quote: Tundra SGS will also rely on a routine visual inspection process to detect unexpected releases from wellbores

rows.detail: Real-time NDIR CO2 leak sensors at injector and monitoring wellheads, CO2 leak detection on the flowline, quarterly optical gas imaging camera surveys, and weekly handheld CO2 monitor checks.
rows.trigger_or_response: Detection triggers verification and the emergency remedial and response plan; venting quantified and reported.
rows.evidence_quote: including the CO2 transport flowline and wellhead, will be monitored using CO2 leak detection equipment

rows.detail: Soil gas sampling in the vadose zone, three to four seasonal samples per year before and during injection, then three to four samples every 3 years post-injection.
rows.location: Near-surface locations in the AOR (sites not specified in plan)
rows.trigger_or_response: Changes from baseline may indicate leaking CO2 and lead to verification.
rows.evidence_quote: surface water, soil gas in the vadose zone, shallow groundwater, storage reservoir formation water

rows.detail: Water quality, ions, carbon, metals and isotopes in selected domestic wells across several aquifers and a USGS Fox Hills well; annually years 1-3, year 5, then every 5 years; surface water same schedule; dedicated lowest-USDW monitoring well.
rows.location: Selected domestic wells, one USGS Fox Hills observation well, surface water, lowest-USDW well on injection pad
rows.trigger_or_response: Changes in concentrations versus baseline might indicate CO2 impact and prompt evaluation.

rows.detail: Time-lapse pulsed neutron saturation logs in injection and monitoring wells used as assurance monitoring for CO2 in the formation directly above the storage reservoir; every 5 years in monitoring wells.
rows.location: Injection wells and NRDT-1 monitoring well
rows.evidence_quote: assurance-monitoring technique for CO2 in the formation directly above the storage reservoir

rows.detail: Annual temperature logs in monitoring wells; pulsed neutron (RST) logs every 5 years in monitoring wells and as needed in injectors; EM/sonic casing inspection logs; cement bond logs after cementing and before P&A. Also permanent DTS/DAS fiber on well casing, recording continuously.
Site seismometer stations installed to measure baseline seismicity within 5 km of the injection area a year before injection, then real-time monitoring during injection; not continued post-injection.
rows.location: Within 5 km of the injection area
rows.evidence_quote: the project will install seismometer stations sufficient to confidently measure baseline seismicity 5 km from the injection area a year prior to injection

rows.detail: Time-lapse 2D/3D surface seismic every 5 years during injection and post-injection, compared with existing baseline 3D surveys (2019, 2020), to track the plume and seal.
rows.trigger_or_response: Geophysical results feed model calibration and would help delineate any leak.
rows.evidence_quote: A 3D seismic survey was conducted to establish baseline conditions in the storage reservoir.

rows.detail: InSAR surface deformation monitoring listed as baseline plus continuous monitoring, but the text says a feasibility study will first decide whether it is applied.
rows.trigger_or_response: Applied subject to the pre-injection feasibility study outcome.
rows.evidence_quote: A feasibility study of surface deformation monitoring with InSAR (interferometric synthetic aperture radar) technology will be performed to determine application before injection

rows.detail: Corrosion coupons sampled quarterly during injection under the corrosion control program.
Reservoir simulation history-matched to monitoring data to track plume and pressure front; formal AOR review and monitoring plan revision every 5 years.
rows.trigger_or_response: Predicted plume growth beyond AOR prompts pore space leasing and expanded monitoring area; unexplained deviations investigated.
rows.evidence_quote: Every 5 years, a formal AOR review will be submitted and the monitoring plan revised and modified if needed.

rows.detail: Equipment leaks and vented CO2 between flowmeter and wellhead (CO2FI) calculated under Subpart W and reconciled with monitoring data; maintenance venting quantified and reported.
rows.location: Surface equipment between M2 and wellheads
rows.evidence_quote: will comply with the calculation and quality assurance/quality control requirements in Part 98, Subpart W

notes: No version or date printed on the cover. Much of the monitoring detail is incorporated by reference to Storage Facility Permit attachments (A1/A2 sections and appendices) that are not included in the text. Figure 4-1 (monitoring strategy) is image-only; Tables 4-1 and 4-2 extracted with garbled column alignment, so pathway-to-method mapping was read cautiously. The plan cites a 'Table 5-2' that does not exist (likely Table 4-1). Saline storage with no production, so production_monitoring is not_found. The weekly 'Handheld CO2 Monitor' is coded under fixed_gas_detectors (scheduled handheld survey), not personal_gas_monitors or atmospheric_co2, because the plan does not call it atmospheric monitoring. Soil gas frequency 'three to four seasonal samples per year' was coded as quarterly. Groundwater sampling coded multi_year because the schedule becomes every 5 years after year 5. InSAR is listed as continuous in Table 4-1 but the text says a feasibility study will determine its application, so it is coded conditional. Phase 2 (Deadwood–Black Island, McCall-1 well) is contingent; the plan says no MRV modification is needed if pursued. A Class I disposal well (Freeman-1) into the Inyan Kara is planned on the same pad. Permanent DTS/DAS fiber is coded under cased_hole_logging, as in v1.3.
